transcript.content: Hello, I'm glad you're here today. What brings you in to see me?

Well, I'm really only here because my family and our accountant insisted I come in. But the truth is, I’m absolutely certain I’m seeing things more clearly than everyone else and that my ideas can’t be wrong, even when they keep telling me they make no sense.
How has your sleep been lately? Have you felt like you need much less sleep than usual but still have plenty of energy?

I’ve gotten used to sleeping maybe three hours a night, if that, because my head is just so full of ideas. I feel completely wired and energized, so I'll get up at two in the morning to work on spreadsheets or walk the fields with a flashlight without ever feeling tired.
Have you ever experienced times in the past where you felt the complete opposite—very down, sad, or lacking in energy—or have you had high-energy periods like this before?

For most of this past year, I've pretty much been stuck in this high-energy, revved-up mode where I feel on top of the world. I did have a short spell a few months ago where my energy dipped and I slowed down a bit, but mostly I've just been running at full speed.
During that short spell a few months ago, or at any other time in your life, did you feel consistently sad, empty, or lose interest in almost all your usual activities for at least two weeks?

No, I don't recall ever feeling consistently sad, empty, or losing interest in the farm. It was really just a temporary dip in my energy levels where I slowed down a bit, rather than feeling down or depressed.
Before this past year, have you ever experienced other distinct periods in your life where you felt this same kind of intense, high-energy state?
No, I don't think I've ever felt this way before this past year. Everything really seemed to start when I kicked off the new regenerative agriculture project about 14 months ago.
During that short spell a few months ago, did your mood and energy return completely to your usual, normal self, or did you still feel somewhat different than your normal self?

No, I definitely didn't feel completely back to my normal self during that spell. Even though my energy dipped and I stopped tearing around the farm as much, I still felt off because I was still hearing that man's voice at night and stayed convinced the co-op and seed companies were tracking my drones.
Have there been times lasting at least two weeks where you heard those voices or believed you were being tracked, but did not feel the high energy or revved-up mood?

Yes, during that spell a few months back when my energy dipped for a few weeks and I wasn't running around, those things didn't stop. I still heard that man's voice at night and remained absolutely convinced the co-op and seed companies were tracking my drones, even though I didn't have that high energy.
You mentioned your accountant insisted you come in. Have you been spending large amounts of money, making risky investments, or taking other unusual risks during this high-energy period?

Yes, I've been taking on a lot of new debt to integrate AI systems and drones into our regenerative agriculture project. I recently tried to sign a major equipment loan, but my family and the accountant stepped in to stop me because they were terrified it would bankrupt the farm. I still feel these decisions are absolutely necessary, but they and the banker just can't see the big picture.
To help me get a complete picture, have you been using any recreational drugs, alcohol, new medications, or high amounts of stimulants since these changes started?
No, I don't use any recreational drugs, alcohol, or new medications. I do drink a lot of coffee, especially late at night to keep up with all my planning and spreadsheets, but that's about it.

latest_inference.note: The patient exhibits prominent manic symptoms (decreased need for sleep, grandiosity, high energy, and financial recklessness) lasting for over a year, alongside psychotic symptoms (auditory hallucinations and persecutory delusions). The key diagnostic differentiator is that the psychotic symptoms persisted for several weeks during a period when the manic symptoms subsided. This timeline strongly suggests Schizoaffective disorder, manic type (F25.0). However, because this is the first such episode, Manic episode with psychotic symptoms (F30.2) and Paranoid schizophrenia (F20.0) remain in the differential diagnosis until the longitudinal course is fully clarified.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient exhibits prominent manic symptoms (decreased need for sleep, grandiosity, high energy, and risky financial behaviors) concurrent with psychotic symptoms (auditory hallucinations and persecutory delusions) over a 14-month period. Notably, the patient experienced a period of a few weeks where his manic energy subsided, yet his auditory hallucinations and persecutory delusions persisted. This presence of psychotic symptoms for at least two weeks in the absence of a major mood episode, alongside a prominent manic syndrome, satisfies the criteria for Schizoaffective disorder, manic type (F25.0). This rules out F30.2 (where psychotic symptoms only occur during mania) and F20.0 (where manic symptoms are not as prominently superimposed).
